result.topic: legs: hanging trestle legs at the EV109 wood bridges and the stacked-copy fix (015-16 feedback)
result.summary: The stack works. A second copy of the same model, placed 5.04 m lower along the model Y axis, gives 0 hanging legs at all 7 wood sites. The upper feet land on the lower copy's kerb beams, the posts line up exactly in plan and nothing overlaps or z-fights. All 7 wood bridges hang today, not just 015-16: 4 to 12 legs each, up to 4.82 m. The 3 metal_25 sites have none. The cost of stacking is a second walkable plank deck inside the gully: 10 to 30 m exposed, 1.0 to 4.6 m above the water. Chernarus has no precedent for this: it stacks none of its 36 wood bridges and keeps its legs on the ground (worst hang 0.2 m). Recommendation: stack at 015-16, 015-18, 015-19, 015-37 and 015-40. At 015-42, swap to the vanilla tall variant bridge_wood_50_1, which leaves 1 leg at 0.14 m and adds no second deck. Do not stack at 015-25: its lower deck would sit only 1.0 m above the water with its side beams in the water. That site needs Guillermo's call. A terrain fill under the legs is not needed with the stack, and cannot replace it, because at every site the worst legs stand over the channel floor. The road texture on the slopes is not caused by cls: at the reserve vertices the cut lowered, cls is 0 or 6. That half of his request needs a different source and owner.
findings: MEASURED (ODOL, members.py -> members.json, models in P:/DZ/structures/roads/bridges): bridge_wood_50 visual LOD 1 has 22 legs (11 rows at x -21.31,-17.76,-13.74,-9.43,-5.10,-0.26,4.56,8.89,13.20,17.22,20.83; z about +-3.5; 0.46 m square). Feet are at y -2.603..-2.524 and post tops at 2.39 or below. Deck planks are at y 2.27..2.41 (x -18.66..18.12) and the kerbs on top are 2.32..2.60 (-z) and 2.33..2.56 (+z). In the geometry LOD, 20 leg components run y -2.511..2.305 and component17 is the deck slab (y 2.07..2.45, x -18.53..17.69). From deck top to foot is 5.05 m.

Its planks span x -9.54..9.56 and its ramps run from about 9.4 to 16.7. Its post spacing equals wood_50's west half shifted by -9.12 m, except the end row at 12.06. bridge_metal_25: 2 piers (geometry components 01/02 at z +-10.81), y -12.415..6.37, roadway 6.37..12.415.

MEASURED: P:/DZ/structures/roads/bridges/bridge_wood_50_1.p3d is a vanilla tall variant of wood_50 with the same plan and ramps. Its roadway and deck sit 1.301 m higher (roadway 1.529..3.747) and its feet are at -3.904..-3.825, so it reaches 7.65 m from deck top to foot, 2.6 m more than wood_50. It has NO centre leg pair: 20 legs. Chernarus uses it once, at (559.8, 418.0, 11220.2), with every leg buried at least 1.0 m.

MEASURED (legs_world.py -> legs-ev109.json; foot = lowest bottom vertex of each visual leg, world = T + R*v from bridge-records.json, planar NW-SE terrain from terrain-ev109.npz): hanging legs (gap > 0.05 m) per site. 015-16 wood_50: 12/22, max 4.12, the centre leg x=-0.26 z=-3.49 foot 5.82 over terrain 1.61. 015-40 wood_50: 12/22, max 4.82. 015-42 wood_50: 8/22, max 3.32. 015-18 wood_25: 8/14, max 3.64. 015-19: 9/14, max 4.13. 015-37: 7/14, max 3.17. 015-25: 4/14, max 1.48. 015-8/11/13 metal_25: 0, piers buried 11.95 to 14.93 m.

MEASURED stack geometry: feet of the upper copy at -2.603..-2.524 against post tops of the lower copy at 2.39 or below and its kerb tops at 2.56/2.60. So the lower offset X must lie in [2.39+2.603, 2.56+2.524] = [4.993, 5.084] m. Below that, the posts overlap coplanar (z-fighting); above it, a light gap opens under the feet. Chosen X = 5.04: the upper feet sink 0.04-0.16 m into the lower kerbs. The posts line up 1:1 in plan, the upper bracing (lowest y -0.40) clears the lower kerbs by about 2 m, and no beams overlap. Cosmetic: on the -z side the feet hang 0.15 m past the kerb's outer edge (post z to -3.72, kerb to -3.57).

MEASURED with the stack at X=5.04 (stack.py -> stack-report.json): lower legs hanging = 0 at all 7 wood sites. Lower feet sit 0.22 m (015-40) to 7.99 m below the terrain. Lower legs inside the channel (1-2 per site) reach 0.18 to 3.52 m below the bed. Lower ramps exposed = 0 m everywhere (buried). Lower roadway world y / height above water / exposed length at the axis: 015-16 5.78 / +4.08 / 26.8 m; 015-40 6.72 / +4.59 / 29.5; 015-42 5.11 / +2.94 / 20.0; 015-18 4.89 / +3.39 / 17.0; 015-19 8.64 / +3.92 / 18.8; 015-37 7.44 / +2.79 / 15.5; 015-25 3.11 / +1.03 / 10.0. Lower x-bracing bottom above water: 015-25 -1.82 (in the water and bed), 015-37 -0.06, 015-42 +0.08, the others +0.54 to +1.75. Lower side beams at 015-25: -0.08 (at the waterline).

MEASURED: the lower copy does not block the engine water or the channel in plan. Its legs stand on the same xz as the upper legs, it is entirely above the pond level except legs and bracing, it changes no terrain, and it adds no seal. It DOES create a second walkable roadway LOD surface (wood planks) over the gully, 10-30 m exposed per site, reachable from the cut slopes. Its bracing frames span across at 1.2-3.5 m above the water and partly block walking along the stream under the bridge.

MEASURED (vanilla.py -> vanilla-wood-bridges.json, data E:/DayZ-Baltic-Build/vanilla-tricks-20261013): Chernarus has 36 bridge_wood_* (33 wood_25, 2 wood_50, 1 wood_50_1) and Livonia has 0. None is stacked: 0 have another road bridge within 4 m in plan. Every leg reaches the terrain: worst hang 0.20 m (wood_25 at 10318.9, 3530.0) and 0.14 m (850.5, 4009.8); the others are buried 0.11-7.55 m. Chernarus solves this by keeping the gully under a wood bridge no deeper than the legs, with streambed objects under the deck. pier_wooden1_pillars (P:/DZ/structures/industrial/harbour) has no roadway LOD, but its 4-post module (about 3.4 x 2.1 m) does not match the bridge leg grid, and neither map uses it.

MEASURED (tall50.py, tall50_fill.py): swapping to bridge_wood_50_1 keeps the roadway exactly where wood_50's is (position moved -1.301 m along model Y). After the swap: 015-42 has 1/20 legs hanging, 0.14 m (within the Chernarus tolerance). 015-16 has 4/20 hanging (0.17, 0.28, 1.29, 1.31). The two 1.3 m legs stand at q=-2.39 and q=+2.02, at the edge of the channel (W/2 = 2.15), and the planar triangle under each includes a channel-floor vertex, so a fill cannot hold them. 015-40 has 6/20 hanging, max 2.22, two of them 2.0 m over the water.

MEASURED (fill.py -> fill-check.json): without a stack, at every wood site at least 2 hanging legs, and at 015-25 all 4, are wet or sit on a planar triangle that includes a channel-floor vertex (|q| <= W/2). A fill outside W cannot hold them on the 6 m grid. With the stack, no fill is needed (0 lower legs hang).

MEASURED (reserve_cut.py): at the cut reserve vertices around each wood site (6 to 23 per site; none at 015-37), cls is 0 (dry) or 6. So cls does not carry a road class there. For the road texture under the deck, the hypothesis 'the reserve cells keep their road class' is false for cls. The texture must come from another layer (the reserve or platform masks or the road raster). Not verified which one. bridge-report.json cut_frozen_vertices: 015-16 26, 015-18 13, 015-19 14, 015-25 13, 015-37 13, 015-40 28, 015-42 24.

INFERRED: wood_25 under wood_50 is worse than a full wood_50 copy. Shifted -9.12 m, it aligns 6 of its 7 post rows, but its end post lands mid-bay (x 2.94) and its +x ramp lands inside the gully at the lower level. The full same-model copy keeps all posts aligned and buries its ramps (0 m exposed). No shift or shortening is recommended.

Code referenced: tools/terrain/bridges_v31.py:50-61 (model_info reads the roadway LOD; the end heights also hold for wood_50_1); :99 and :108 (matrix columns X, Y, Z then position; Rm columns); :103-110 (records loop, where a stack record belongs); :116 (flat = half_all - 6.5); :155 and :160-163 (bank target, deck footprint, allowed = zone & (~frozen | |sroad| <= flat): the cut through the whole reserve band that makes the gully); :19-25 (corridor rationale). proposal: Recommended (G5, simplest that covers each site): 015-16 and 015-40: stack a second bridge_wood_50 5.04 m lower, as Guillermo asked (wood_50_1 alone leaves 1.3 m and 2.2 m hangs there). 015-18, 015-19 and 015-37: stack a second bridge_wood_25 5.04 m lower. 015-42: replace the upper copy with bridge_wood_50_1 (1 leg at 0.14 m, no second deck, Chernarus precedent); stacking also works there if he prefers one solution everywhere (lower deck +2.94 m over the water, bracing +0.08 m at the waterline). 015-25: do not stack; ask him whether to accept 4 legs hanging 0.45-1.48 m or stack anyway with a deck 1.0 m above the water. metal_25 sites: no change.

[DESIGN] Implementation in tools/terrain/bridges_v31.py: add an optional site field 'stack' (bool) and an optional 'model' swap to bridge_wood_50_1 in the sites JSON. In the records loop (bridges_v31.py:103-110), after appending the span record, when s.get('stack') append a second record with the same X, Y, Z and position pos - 5.04*Y (Y = the model-up column u), role 'stack-lower'. Derive the stack from the final pose; do not freeze the prototype matrices, because the bridge-end workflow may change h1/h2. The model swap needs no code: model_info reads wood_50_1's roadway (ends 1.529) and the pose code keeps the roadway at road grade.

[DESIGN] Constant to add next to BANK, CUT_T, etc.: STACK_DY = 5.04, documented as 'upper feet -2.603..-2.524 rest on lower kerbs 2.56/2.60; valid range 4.993..5.084'. Add a report field per site: lower legs hanging (must be 0), lower roadway above water, lower bracing above water. Gate: hanging lower legs == 0, lower roadway above water >= 2.0 m (this rejects 015-25), measured with legs_world-style feet against the final terrain.

No terrain fill under the legs. If a smaller second deck is wanted later, the lever is the bank slope under the deck (BANK 0.5 at bridges_v31.py:155): a steeper bank buries more of the lower deck. That is a terrain change, to be coordinated with the bridge-end workflow, and it is not needed for the legs.

Road texture on the cut slopes (the other half of his request): it does not come from cls (0/6 at the cut reserve vertices). The texture or surface owner (or the bridge-end workflow, if it owns the wing slopes) must find which layer paints road there (reserve/platform mask or the road raster) and clear it for the vertices in v31_bridge_cut. This workflow does not change it.

Prototype records in my folder: stack-records.json (all 7 wood sites, bridge-records.json format plus role and offset_model_y) and proposed-records.json (the recommended set: 5 stack-lower adds and the 015-42 wood_50_1 replace). Side elevations before and after: side-<site>.png, side-all.png, and side-<site>-wood_50_1.png for the 3 wood_50 sites.

risks: Dependency on the bridge-end workflow (wf-bridge-end/endfit.py, in progress; no final output read). It may change the end pose (h1/h2) or raise terrain at the ends. Raising terrain only buries more of the lower copy, which is harmless. A pose change moves the upper matrix, so the stack must be generated inside bridges_v31 from the final pose (pos - 5.04*Y), not from my prototype matrices. Both changes must go into one bridges_v31 run.

Second walkable deck: the lower roadway LOD (wood planks) is exposed 10-30 m per stacked site and reachable from the cut slopes. Its bracing frames cut across the gully 1.2-3.5 m above the water, partly blocking walking along the stream under the bridge. Neither vanilla map has a precedent for this. Guillermo should judge it in game.

015-25: stacking there yields a deck 1.0 m above the water with its side beams at the waterline. If he wants a stack everywhere, that site will look like a low footbridge. 015-37 and 015-42: the lower bracing sits at the waterline (-0.06 / +0.08).

015-40 with the stack: the shallowest lower foot is only 0.22 m below the terrain. If any later terrain pass lowers that slope (for example the wing slopes), it could hang again. Re-measure feet after any terrain change.

bridge_wood_50_1 at 015-42 removes the centre leg pair and changes the model from the one placed and reviewed in EV109. The end ramps are the same shape relative to the road (roadway offset 1.301 in both roadway and deck), but the bridge-end census should be re-run for that site.
The heights are measured on the planar NW-SE triangles of terrain-ev109.npz, not in game. Real foot contact on 0.04-0.16 m kerb embeds was not seen in the renderer.
unverified: Not verified in game (no DayZ MCP use): what the two-tier trestle looks like, whether light shows between the feet and the kerbs, and whether the 0.15 m overhang of the -z feet past the kerb edge is visible.

Not verified: engine behaviour of the lower copy's roadway LOD where it is buried under the terrain (ramps fully, deck ends partly). Expected harmless (the terrain is the highest surface), but not tested; same for navmesh and AI pathing over the lower deck.
Not verified: which layer paints the road texture on the cut slopes. Only measured that cls is 0/6 there, not a road class.
Not verified: whether the Sakhal bridge_wood2_pillar (P:/DZ/structures_sakhal, 12 m pillars) can be used without a Frostline DLC dependency. It was not considered as an option for that reason.
The legs were measured with the visual LOD 1 pieces. Geometry LOD feet are at -2.511 (wood) vs -2.6 visual, so collision feet are 0.09 m higher than drawn; not separately tabulated.
The 7 renders were looked at for 015-16, 015-25 and 015-42 only; the others were generated by the same code but not inspected image by image.

result.summary: La textura de carretera que se ve bajo los puentes NO viene de cls ni de reserve. Viene de las capas satélite y máscara de EV95, que se pintaron cuando el terraplén seguía entero y que se envían congeladas: package_ev109.py solo cambia el WRP. La pintura es una franja de 7 m (≤3,5 m de la cadena de carretera, ranura 0 = cp_gravel, tono ROAD_RGB), así que tras el corte de bridges_v31 recorre todo el barranco bajo el tablero. Medido en EV109: 2.585 px de 1 m de pintura de carretera sobre terreno rebajado >0,5 m en los 11 sitios con corte (pilot 015-15 + 10 del rollout). En 015-16 son 324 px (295 bajo el tablero) con hasta 6,98 m de rebaje; en kits y en los 8 puentes de Narva, 0. Cambio mínimo: una opción en build_surface_v30.py que apaga la carretera en las celdas que tocan v31_bridge_cut. Después se regeneran solo las 22 teselas afectadas con los flags de EV95 y el plano de agua de EV109, se componen sobre los PNG fuente de EV95 solo dentro de esas celdas (+2 px), se pasan a PAA (44 ficheros) y el empaquetado los añade a las entradas cambiadas. Prototipo en 015-16: la pintura de carretera rebajada pasa de 324 px a 0. El barranco toma la superficie natural del entorno (cp_conifer_common1 en las orillas secas y cp_gravel de lecho/orilla en el cauce), que es lo que hace Chernarus bajo sus tableros.
